chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Nahdi, from Ibn Abi Najran, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever buys a stolen item while he knows it is stolen, he has shared in its disgrace and its sin."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying stolen goods if you know they are stolen?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on earnings, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the principle of *shirkah* (partnership) in guilt, extending moral liability beyond the thief to the knowing buyer. It serves as a foundational legal maxim in Shia jurisprudence for invalidating transactions involving stolen property, emphasizing that commercial gain derived from injustice carries shared spiritual and social disgrace.
